definition: Remedial means intended to correct or improve weak skills in a specific area, especially basic ones.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word remedial. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know remedial should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Twice a week, the third graders in the remedial reading program meet with a tutor who rebuilds their phonics skills step by step.
A refresher course is weaker than a remedial one; a refresher lightly reviews what students already know, while a remedial course rebuilds skills that never took hold.
Intensive is stronger than remedial; a remedial class fixes weak basics at a steady pace, while an intensive program is a demanding, immersive overhaul of a subject.

Corrective means aimed at fixing any identified fault or error, and it is the standard word after inspections and audits — a corrective action plan. Remedial lives in the classroom: it describes instruction that repairs weak basic skills. Faults get corrective steps; skill gaps get remedial lessons.

Foundational describes the most basic level of a subject — foundational math is where everyone starts. It says nothing about anything having gone wrong. Remedial is basic content with a mission: it exists because specific skills never took hold and must be rebuilt.

Catch-up work helps someone reach the level the rest of the group has already reached — extra sessions after a long absence, say. Remedial instruction is more diagnostic: it goes back and rebuilds specific weak skills, usually basic ones, rather than just covering missed ground.

After three fender benders in the parking lot, the delivery company enrolled its newest drivers in a remedial driving course that drilled mirror checks and slow-speed turns.
The course exists for one reason: to fix the basic driving skills these drivers clearly never mastered.
Instruction designed to correct a specific weakness in fundamental skills is exactly what remedial describes.
Most common in education: remedial classes, remedial instruction, remedial lessons.
Formal writing does sometimes use remedial action for steps taken to fix a problem, but after an inspection or audit the standard phrase is corrective action, not remedial.
Do not confuse remedial with elementary, which describes content that is simply basic, not content specifically designed to repair a skill gap.

Dev aced shop class and could rebuild a carburetor blindfolded, but the community college placement test flagged his writing.
Somewhere back in middle school, the rules for building a paragraph had never taken hold, and every essay since had been a guess.
The college's answer was a remedial writing course: eight weeks, no credit, nothing but the basics he had missed.
The instructor did not review -- she rebuilt.
Topic sentences, then evidence, then transitions, each skill drilled until it held.
In October, Dev turned in his first real term paper.
It came back with one comment in the margin: 'Nothing to fix here.'
